Timeline::week¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Series Timeline::week() const

week() is the sole public spelling.

Read The ISO Week Number¶

week() returns the ISO week number of each local date as shape-preserving int32. ISO weeks begin on Monday and are numbered 1 through 53. Week 1 is the week containing the year’s first Thursday, so the week-number boundary does not always coincide with 1 January. Absent instants return -1.

This convention explains an initially surprising but correct result: Friday, 1 January 2021 belongs to ISO week 53 of the preceding ISO week-year.

Example: A Civil-Year Boundary Inside One ISO Week¶

const auto events = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2020-12-31T23:59:59.123456789Z",
    "2021-01-01T00:00:00.987654321Z",
    "2024-02-29T06:07:08.009010011Z",
    "",
});

pluss::series::print(std::cout, events.week());

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=int32, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[53, 53, 9, -1]

The first two timestamps have different year() values but the same ISO week number. That contrast is the central rule to remember.

Constructing Week-Based Keys Safely¶

Do not assume (year(), week()) is a valid ISO year-week key around New Year: the civil year returned by year() and the ISO week-numbering year can differ. If your application needs a globally unambiguous weekly key, define and retain the week boundary itself, or explicitly compute the matching week-year under the application’s calendar policy.

For weekday position within the ISO week, weekday() uses the compatible Monday-zero convention.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Weeks begin on Monday, not Sunday.

  • A year can contain week 53.

  • The local timezone determines the date and therefore the week.

  • week() returns only the number, not the corresponding week-year.

  • -1 means the source was NaT.

Summary¶

Use week() for ISO-style weekly grouping after choosing the correct local timezone. Treat New Year as a real calendar boundary case, not an exception to ignore, and never pair the number blindly with the civil year.
